threads.body: [Testing] The old-semconv branch only proves that the value is some string other than the registry target, so it would still pass if the provider-host restoration returned any incorrect address. Since setup forces Dubbo's local address to the loopback address, assert that exact resolved provider host to lock in the regression this PR fixes.

replies.body: Good catch. The exact resolved provider host turned out to be environment-dependent — locally it resolves to the machine's real LAN IP (e.g. `10.0.0.187`) rather than the forced loopback, and it differs again on CI runners, so asserting an exact host would be flaky. I've strengthened the old-semconv assertion to `asString().isNotEqualTo(expectedServerAddress).doesNotContain("/")`, which locks in that `server.address` is a bare provider host and not a registry url/target (the registry target always contains `/`). This also surfaced and fixed a related gap: under old semconv the client `server.address` reverts to the provider host, so `peer.service` now resolves on the client span under latest deps — added that assertion too.
